Planning permission for the mixed-use redevelopment of London Dock was originally granted on 24 March 2014 (the “Original Permission”), allowing for the delivery of up to 1,800 residential units. This consent approved a range of residential buildings and associated works, with full planning permission granted for Buildings A, B, C, Times House and the Pennington Street Warehouse (PSW), and outline permission secured for Plots D, E, F, G, H and J. The permission was accompanied by Listed Building Consent (LPA ref. PA/13/01277) authorising works to the Grade II listed PSW.
Subsequently, on 12 January 2015, a Section 73 application (LPA ref. PA/14/02819) was approved (“the 2015 Permission”). This consent allowed amendments to the design and layout of Buildings C1 and C2/C3, together with changes to the associated landscaping, enabling the early release of 85 residential units from the outline element of the Original Permission.
Further amendments were approved on 5 March 2018 through another Section 73 application (LPA ref. PA/17/02112), known as the London Dock Hybrid Planning Permission (“LDHPP”). These revisions focused on design improvements, modifications to internal layouts, and adjustments to the residential mix within Building C1.
In parallel, a new Listed Building Consent (LPA ref. PA/17/02826) was granted on 9 March 2018. This consent consolidated all previously approved works to the PSW and introduced a series of additional alterations.
A third Section 73 application (LPA ref. PA/19/00764) was submitted in April 2019, with planning permission subsequently granted.
On 11 October 2019, a Section 96a application was submitted to allow further internal and external amendments to the PSW. At the same time, a revised Listed Building Consent application was made for the Grade II listed PSW, incorporating all previously approved alterations alongside additional changes. Consent was issued on 10 March 2020, subject to a number of planning conditions, several of which required discharge prior to the commencement of works.
This current application reflects the most up-to-date consented scheme for “Area 1” of the Pennington Street Warehouse. These approved proposals have informed the design principles underpinning the present Listed Building Consent application, which also includes limited refinements to the refurbishment and internal fit-out.
description: Listed Building Consent for internal fit-out works to Area 1, comprising the continuation of previously permitted internal alterations, including the construction of a mezzanine level; installation of toilets and a kitchen; associated drainage and electrical services; formation of a new screeded floor incorporating underfloor heating connected to the consented district heat network; installation of two new steel and concrete staircases; and repair works to internal stone cills.
